params.body:
First step of "Elixir for agents: the measurement is the unit, and Elixir judges". Until now Portal's cards held the judgement: 29 PHP methods turned facts into now/week/month, 13 with numbers hardcoded in PHP, while `Thresholds.php` was meant to be the one registry of judgement numbers. Two judges, and agents reading a screen's vocabulary.

- `Level` (now, week, month, background, ok; ranked) and `Verdict` (`{facet, level, threshold, reason}`), built only from a threshold in the registry that names a level; unknown or level-less thresholds are refused.
- `Judged`: a measurement names the thresholds it judges by (`judgements()`) and turns facts into verdicts (`judge()`). Deterministic, no prose.
- `Outcome::withVerdicts()` and `level()`; verdicts ride only on a measured outcome.
- `Thresholds`: entries may carry `level`; `DEPLOYED_CURRENT` ok, `DEPLOYED_BEHIND` month, new `DEPLOYED_STALLED_WEEK` (2 days) week and `DEPLOYED_STALLED` (7 days) now. Same numbers as Portal's card.
- `Deployed` implements `Judged` (facet `behind`); `Measure` writes `verdicts` under each key and under staging; `elixir:publish-catalog` publishes `judgements` per key.

Additive: Portal ignores the new field until its own PR reads it. Suite 567 green, PHPStan green.

Proposed through the control gateway under #agent-workbench.
params.title: The measurement judges: Level, Verdict, Judged, and Deployed as the first judge
